reason: I read labels and care about third-party testing, and a named lab with a report per batch is what I'd normally have to dig for. Magnesium bisglycinate with no oxide, one sachet in the gym bag for travel weeks, and the launch price of $24.99 with an empty-box refund makes one box a low-risk try.
objection: $29.99 is more than Toplux or Goli and I have to see that the lab report is real, names the lab, and matches the 200 mg on the label before I pay. Two capsules a day for 30 days is not cheap for a brand I have never heard of.
would_change_my_mind: If the lab report were missing, from an unnamed lab, or showed a different magnesium amount than 200 mg elemental, I would not buy. I would also pass if the price after the launch offer stayed at $29.99 and I had no reviews to read.
